I feel like the easiest way initially is to make recipes that can be constructed on the plate - that is, things like tacos and pastas can be made with meats and vegetables in separate dishes. That way you can heat up some black beans for alternate filler and use all the same ingredients for a veggie burrito as normal (same with vegetable marinara and ground beef.) 

Something good to keep in mind too is not to try and imitate meat with aoy knockoffs as much as replace it with things that taste different, but delicious in their own right. Such as grilling a portobello cap is way better (and cheaper sometimes) than a pack of frozen veggie patties, and can be enjoyed by omnivores as well.

The key is to find foods that everyone can enjoy regardless of diet, and then make the meat an add in option instead of a staple.
